_comment: What a non-2xx answer from the usage endpoint means, in one contract every port shares. `signInAgain` (401 only) is the only outcome no amount of retrying fixes: the credentials themselves are finished, so the panels must stop drawing that account's bars as if they were current and say so instead. `retryable` keeps the last good reading up while the next poll tries again. `label` names a saved account in the message; without one the message is the LIVE login's, and it carries the refresh hint - clients never write that token, so Claude Code's own refresh is the only cure. Pinned across lib/pure/usage.js (GNOME), claude-code/normalize.js (CLI + MCP + status line) and ClaudeUsageCore/HttpFailure.swift (macOS). A 403 is `forbidden`, not expired: the token is valid but not allowed this endpoint (a setup-token without the user:profile scope answers permission_error), so no refresh cures it and the server's own words are shown instead of the refresh hint. `retryAfter` is the raw Retry-After header (delta-seconds or an HTTP-date, read against `now`); a transient answer carries `retryAfterSeconds` only when it was usable, and nothing else ever does.
authExpiredMessage: Claude session expired. Run any Claude Code command to refresh it.

503 with an HTTP-date Retry-After is read against now

a Retry-After that is neither form is ignored
a fractional Retry-After is ignored too
only a transient answer carries a wait: a 404 with Retry-After has none
